name: Planetary Data System
blurb: NASA's archive for every planetary mission it has flown. Not one repository but a federation: seven discipline nodes that curate the science, plus an Engineering Node that owns the standard, the registry and the tools. Everything in it is public domain, with no account and no fee.

children.name: Cartography & Imaging Sciences Node
children.blurb: The pictures, and the map products made from them. By volume this is most of the archive: one camera, HiRISE, outweighs several whole nodes.

children.name: HiRISE
children.note: 25 cm/pixel from orbit. The single largest instrument archive in the PDS.

children.name: CTX context camera
children.note: 6 m/pixel, now covering essentially the whole planet.

children.name: MARCI weather camera
children.note: Daily global weather imaging, the basis of the Mars weather report.

children.name: Mars Orbiter Camera
children.note: Mars Global Surveyor. The first modern high-resolution look at the surface.

children.name: Viking Orbiter imaging
children.note: Vidicon frames, restored and reprocessed several times since.

children.name: Mars 2020 cameras
children.note: Mastcam-Z, Navcam, SHERLOC WATSON, plus the Ingenuity helicopter cameras.

children.name: MSL Curiosity cameras
children.note: Mastcam, MAHLI, MARDI, Navcam and Hazcam.

children.name: MER Pancam & Navcam
children.note: Spirit and Opportunity, fourteen years of them.

children.name: InSight IDC & ICC
children.note: Arm and body cameras that documented the instrument deployment.

children.name: Mars Pathfinder IMP
children.note: The imager that gave us the first color panoramas from the surface since Viking.

children.name: LROC NAC & WAC
children.note: Narrow and wide angle cameras on Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.

children.name: Apollo metric & panoramic scans
children.note: Film from the J-mission service modules, scanned at high resolution.

children.name: Lunar Orbiter frames
children.note: Recovered from analog tape decades later and digitized.

children.name: Clementine UVVIS & NIR
children.note: The first global multispectral map of the Moon.

children.name: Cassini ISS
children.note: Thirteen years of Saturn, its rings and its moons.

children.name: Voyager ISS
children.note: The only close imaging of Uranus and Neptune that exists.

children.name: Galileo SSI
children.note: Small by modern standards because the high-gain antenna never opened.

children.name: JunoCam
children.note: A public-outreach camera whose raw frames are processed by volunteers.

children.name: New Horizons LORRI & Ralph
children.note: Returned over sixteen months on a link measured in kilobits.

children.name: Magellan SAR
children.note: Radar through the cloud deck, still the best global map of Venus.

children.name: MESSENGER MDIS
children.note: The first orbital imaging of Mercury.

children.name: Mariner 10 imaging
children.note: Three flybys, one gravity assist, the whole template for the technique.

children.name: Cartographic map products
children.note: Controlled mosaics and DEMs. Many derived products live at USGS Astrogeology rather than in the PDS proper.

children.name: Geosciences Node
children.blurb: Everything about the solid body: topography, gravity, spectroscopy, in-situ chemistry, seismology. Also hosts the Radio Science subnode and laboratory spectral libraries.

children.name: CRISM hyperspectral
children.note: 544 wavelengths per pixel. How most Martian aqueous minerals were found.

children.name: MOLA topography
children.note: The laser altimetry grid nearly every Mars map is registered to.

children.name: TES thermal spectra
children.note: Mars Global Surveyor. Surface mineralogy plus atmospheric dust and ice.

children.name: Odyssey GRS & neutron spectrometer
children.note: Found the near-surface hydrogen that implied buried ice.

children.name: MSL ChemCam, APXS, CheMin
children.note: Laser spectroscopy, X-ray fluorescence and X-ray diffraction from a rover deck.

children.name: Mars 2020 PIXL, SHERLOC, SuperCam
children.note: Fine-scale elemental and organic mapping tied to the cached samples.

children.name: InSight SEIS & HP3
children.note: The first seismic network on another planet, and the mole that never dug.

children.name: MER Mossbauer, APXS, Mini-TES
children.note: The instruments that identified hematite and jarosite at Meridiani.

children.name: LOLA altimetry
children.note: The densest topographic dataset for any body other than Earth.

children.name: Diviner radiometer
children.note: Surface temperatures, including the coldest places measured in the solar system.

children.name: Moon Mineralogy Mapper
children.note: Chandrayaan-1. Detected hydroxyl and water across the lunar surface.

children.name: GRAIL gravity fields
children.note: Twin spacecraft ranging to each other, producing the crustal thickness map.

children.name: Apollo passive seismic
children.note: Eight years of moonquakes, restored from the original tapes.

children.name: Apollo sample & surface experiments
children.note: Sample measurements and ALSEP data, still being reprocessed.

children.name: MESSENGER MASCS, MLA, gravity
children.note: Spectroscopy, laser altimetry and the gravity field of the innermost planet.

children.name: Magellan gravity & altimetry
children.note: Still the reference gravity model for Venus, thirty years on.

children.name: Radio Science subnode
children.note: Gravity fields and atmospheric occultations derived from the tracking link itself.

children.name: RELAB & spectral libraries
children.note: Measured spectra of real minerals and meteorites. The ground truth remote sensing is matched against.

children.name: Atmospheres Node
children.blurb: Every atmosphere in the solar system except Earth's: weather, composition, structure, escape. Small in bytes, long in time series.

children.name: MAVEN IUVS, NGIMS & remote sensing
children.note: The mission built to measure how Mars lost its air.

children.name: Mars Climate Sounder
children.note: Limb profiles of temperature, dust and water ice through the whole column.

children.name: MSL REMS
children.note: A decade of daily surface weather from one location in Gale crater.

children.name: InSight APSS & TWINS
children.note: Pressure at 20 Hz, which turned out to record passing dust devils and impacts.

children.name: MGS TES atmospheric products
children.note: Global dust and temperature records spanning several Mars years.

children.name: Cassini CIRS
children.note: Composite infrared spectra of Saturn, Titan and the icy moons.

children.name: Juno MWR
children.note: Microwave sounding hundreds of kilometers below the visible cloud tops.

children.name: Voyager IRIS
children.note: The infrared spectra still cited for Uranus and Neptune.

children.name: Galileo Probe
children.note: Fifty-eight minutes of direct measurement before the probe was crushed.

children.name: Huygens DISR & HASI
children.note: The only descent and landing data from an outer solar system body.

children.name: Pioneer Venus orbiter & probes
children.note: Four probes into the atmosphere plus fourteen years in orbit.

children.name: Venus Express (ESA mirror)
children.note: Mirrored from ESA's Planetary Science Archive under a data exchange agreement.

children.name: Ground-based planetary spectra
children.note: IRTF and other telescope data archived as mission support.

children.name: Occultation & photometry archives
children.note: Stellar occultations that probe atmospheric structure from Earth.

children.name: Navigation & Ancillary Information Facility
children.blurb: SPICE: where the spacecraft was, where it was pointing, and how the target body was oriented at that instant. Tiny by volume and load-bearing for everything else. You cannot do geometry on any other node's data without it.

children.name: SPK ephemerides
children.note: Positions and velocities of spacecraft, planets, satellites and small bodies.

children.name: CK pointing
children.note: Instrument and spacecraft attitude through time, reconstructed after the fact.

children.name: DSK shape kernels
children.note: Digital shape models for bodies too irregular to treat as an ellipsoid.

children.name: PCK planetary constants
children.note: Radii, rotation rates and pole orientations, versioned as the values are revised.

children.name: IK & FK definitions
children.note: Instrument fields of view and the reference frame tree that connects them.

children.name: SCLK & LSK clocks
children.note: Spacecraft clock correlation and leapseconds. Time is not simple out there.

children.name: CSPICE, SPICELIB, Icy, Mice
children.note: The reference implementation in C, Fortran, IDL and MATLAB.

children.name: SpiceyPy
children.note: Community Python wrapper, now how most new users reach SPICE.

children.name: WebGeocalc & Cosmographia
children.note: Browser geometry calculator and a 3D visualizer for checking your answer.

children.name: SPICE lessons & tutorials
children.note: NAIF teaches the toolkit directly. The training material is part of the archive.

children.name: Planetary Plasma Interactions Node
children.blurb: Fields and particles: magnetometers, plasma analyzers, energetic particle detectors, radio and plasma wave receivers. Continuous time series rather than scenes.

children.name: Cassini MAG, CAPS, MIMI, RPWS
children.note: The most complete magnetospheric record of any planet but Earth.

children.name: Juno MAG, Waves, JADE, JEDI
children.note: Polar orbits through the auroral field lines, which no earlier mission flew.

children.name: Galileo MAG, PLS, PWS, EPD
children.note: The Europa magnetic signature that implied a conducting subsurface ocean.

children.name: MAVEN MAG, SWIA, SWEA, STATIC, SEP
children.note: Escape rates measured ion species by ion species.

children.name: MGS magnetometer & electron reflectometer
children.note: Found the crustal magnetic stripes in the southern highlands.

children.name: Pioneer Venus plasma & fields
children.note: A solar cycle and a half of an unmagnetized planet in the solar wind.

children.name: ARTEMIS at the Moon
children.note: Two repurposed THEMIS spacecraft, now in lunar orbit.

children.name: Lunar Prospector MAG & ER
children.note: Mapped lunar crustal magnetism and the swirls associated with it.

children.name: Voyager MAG, PLS, PWS
children.note: Still returning data from interstellar space, still being archived.

children.name: Ring-Moon Systems Node
children.blurb: Rings and the small moons that shepherd them. The smallest node by volume and the best search interface in the whole federation: OPUS lets you query by observing geometry, not just by filename.

children.name: Cassini radio science occultations
children.note: Radio through the rings at three wavelengths, resolving structure to tens of meters.

children.name: Cassini UVIS stellar occultations
children.note: A star watched through the rings, sampled fast enough to see individual ringlets.

children.name: Cassini VIMS occultations
children.note: The infrared counterpart, sensitive to particle size.

children.name: Voyager PPS & UVS occultations
children.note: The first high-resolution ring profiles ever obtained.

children.name: Earth-based stellar occultations
children.note: How the Uranian rings were discovered, from an airborne telescope.

children.name: Cassini ISS ring observations
children.note: Reindexed by ring geometry rather than by spacecraft sequence.

children.name: Voyager ring imaging
children.note: Includes the only images of the Neptune ring arcs.

children.name: Hubble ring & satellite programs
children.note: Long-baseline monitoring that catches slow changes missions cannot.

children.name: New Horizons ring search
children.note: A null result that still constrains what is there.

children.name: Ring feature & orbit catalogs
children.note: Derived positions of gaps, ringlets and shepherding moons.

children.name: OPUS search interface
children.note: Faceted search across missions by observing geometry, phase angle and target.

children.name: Ephemeris & geometry generators
children.note: Viewer tools that draw what a ring system looked like from a given place and time.

children.name: Small Bodies Node
children.host: University of Maryland & Planetary Science Institute
children.blurb: Asteroids, comets, dust and returned samples, plus the Minor Planet Center as a subnode. The most heterogeneous holdings in the PDS: spacecraft data sits beside century-old ground-based catalogs.

children.name: OSIRIS-REx OCAMS, OVIRS, OTES, OLA
children.note: Two years of survey before touching the surface for five seconds.

children.name: OSIRIS-REx sample analysis
children.note: Laboratory results on the returned material, archived alongside the remote sensing.

children.name: Hayabusa & Hayabusa2 (JAXA mirror)
children.note: Mirrored from JAXA's DARTS archive.

children.name: Stardust & Stardust-NExT
children.note: The first cometary coma sample returned to Earth.

children.name: Dawn FC, VIR, GRaND
children.note: The only mission to orbit two different bodies, on ion propulsion.

children.name: Rosetta (ESA PSA mirror)
children.note: Two years alongside a comet through perihelion, plus the Philae lander.

children.name: Lucy L'LORRI, L'TES, L'Ralph
children.note: Early main-belt encounters ahead of the Trojan tour.

children.name: DART DRACO & LICIACube
children.note: The final frames before impact, and the cubesat that watched the plume.

children.name: Deep Impact & EPOXI
children.note: An impactor into a comet nucleus, then an extended mission to a second one.

children.name: NEAR Shoemaker
children.note: First orbit of an asteroid, and an unplanned soft landing at the end.

children.name: NEOWISE detections
children.note: Infrared detections that give diameters and albedos, not just orbits.

children.name: Minor Planet Center (subnode)
children.note: Astrometry and orbits for every known small body. Continuously updated.

children.name: Asteroid taxonomy & spectral surveys
children.note: SMASS, S3OS2 and their successors: the spectral classes the field still uses.

children.name: Lightcurve database & shape models
children.note: Rotation periods and inverted shapes, largely from amateur observers.

children.name: Albedo & diameter catalogs
children.note: IRAS and WISE-derived physical properties.

children.name: Cometary photometry & astrometry
children.note: Including plate-era observations digitized into a usable series.

children.name: Interplanetary dust & meteors
children.note: In-situ dust detectors from Ulysses, Galileo and Cassini.

children.name: Engineering Node
children.blurb: No science data at all. The Engineering Node owns the information model, the registry, the search API and the tools every other node runs. This is the part of the PDS that decides what counts as an archive.

children.name: PDS4 Information Model
children.note: An ontology, versioned in a 1.x series, from which the schemas are generated.

children.name: XML schemas & Schematron
children.note: A label either validates or it does not. No human judgment in the loop.

children.name: Discipline & mission dictionaries
children.note: Local data dictionaries let a mission extend the model without forking it.

children.name: Standards Reference & Provider's Handbook
children.note: What a data provider actually has to deliver, and in what shape.

children.name: PDS Registry
children.note: The index of every product, collection, bundle and context object, by LIDVID.

children.name: PDS Search API
children.note: REST and JSON with an OpenAPI spec. The programmatic way in.

children.name: pds.nasa.gov portal
children.note: The human front door, plus per-node portals with their own search tools.

children.name: Validate
children.note: Checks a delivery against the model before a peer review ever sees it.

children.name: Harvest & Registry Manager
children.note: Crawls an accepted archive and loads it into the registry.

children.name: Transform
children.note: Converts archived products into working formats such as GeoTIFF or PNG.

children.name: Deep Archive
children.note: Builds the OAIS submission and archive packages delivered to NSSDCA.
